title: No vision grasps Him
hookLine: eyes do not comprehend Him, and He comprehends all vision (6:103)

lines: TRY TO SEE YOUR OWN EYES.
THE OCEAN ENDS AT THE HORIZON.
cards: Try to see your own eyes. Not in a mirror; directly. You can't.
The thing you see with is the one thing you can never look at. Now try the other way: take in the whole ocean from a beach. Your eyes give up at the horizon.
Sight is a wonderful tool, with edges on both sides. Surah six has just walked through stars, seeds and dawn, all things you can see. Then verse one-oh-three names the one thing sight can't reach.

teach.h: ADRAKA — TO REACH AND TAKE IN.
teach.b: In Pickthall's words: “Vision comprehendeth Him not, but He comprehendeth (all) vision. He is the Subtile, the Aware.” The verb is adraka: to reach, to overtake, to take in completely.
Eyes don't catch up with Allah; Allah catches up with every eye. The two names at the end fit.
Al-Latif: the subtle, so fine He passes beneath notice, and also the gentle. Al-Khabir: the one who knows the inside of things. This verse has a long history in Muslim thought.

Aishah, wife of the Prophet ﷺ, recited it when asked whether he had seen his Lord; her answer, in Bukhari, was no, though other companions, Ibn Abbas among them, are reported to have held a different view.
Scholars also asked about the next life.

teach.h: WILL HE BE SEEN? THE SCHOOLS DIFFER.
teach.b: Sunni theologians of the Ash'ari and Athari schools hold that believers will see Allah in the hereafter, citing a verse in surah seventy-five about faces looking toward their Lord, and a hadith comparing it to seeing the moon.
They read today's verse as saying eyes can't encompass Him, not that they can never see.
Mu'tazili theologians and Twelver Shia scholars read it as ruling out seeing God with eyes at all, and understand those other texts another way.
The schools differ. The second half is not where the argument lies: He takes in every eye.
The hadith of Jibril describes ihsan as worshipping Allah as though you see Him, and if you don't see Him, knowing that He sees you.

how: Muslims cite 6:103 in teaching that Allah is beyond physical sight, and the hadith of Jibril's definition of ihsan, worship as though you see Him, for He sees you, is often taught alongside it on sincerity in prayer.

o: to look upward in prayer toward the open sky
to be blinded by a light too bright to bear
to reach and take in completely, as eyes can't Allah

games.q: inside the verse — tap the pairs.
p: to reach and take in completely
the one who knows the inside
as though you see Him; He sees you

s: Aishah recited 6:103 about the Night Journey
asked whether the Prophet saw his Lord, she said no and cited this verse (Bukhari).
all Muslim schools agree on whether Allah will be seen in the hereafter
Ash'ari and Athari Sunni scholars say believers will see Him; Mu'tazili and Twelver Shia scholars read it differently.
the verse says Allah takes in every eye
its second half: He comprehendeth (all) vision.

games.q: you're asked what ihsan means. what did the Prophet answer Jibril?
o: to know every ruling of the law.
to worship Allah as though you see Him, and if not, He sees you.
games.why: worship Allah as though you see Him; and if you don't see Him, He sees you (the hadith of Jibril, Bukhari and Muslim).

practice: Close your eyes, and notice what changes when your main way of taking in the world switches off: maybe the room sounds louder, maybe your body feels heavier.
Then rest in the verse's second half: eyes don't reach Him, and He reaches every eye, not as a camera or a judge on a screen, but as the Subtle, the gentle one, and the Aware, who knows the inside.

wordCard.voice: Adraka, to reach, to take in completely. Eyes don't take Allah in, but He takes in every eye: the Subtle, the Aware. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: eyes do not reach Him (6:103).

carryVoice: Your line: seen by the unseen. The One who sees is the Subtle, the gentle. See you tomorrow.
